purpose: Read-only audit of the native Word RTF write-reservation hash, its typed-reader boundary, and the corresponding native DOC and DOCX modify-password records.

provenance.authoring_method: Computer Use / native Microsoft Word UI
provenance.source_workflow: Native Word opened word-encrypted.doc with the existing Office42! credential for opening and modification. Save As RTF produced word-write-reservation.rtf.

save_as_warning.description: Native Word displayed an explicit protection-loss warning while saving the encrypted DOC as RTF.
save_as_warning.exact_text: This document is password protected. Saving this document in a format other than a Word Document will result in the loss of this protection. Do you want to continue?

provenance.analysis_method: Read-only hash, raw-control, textutil, in-memory typed-reader, and temporary-copy isolation probes

files.role: native Word Save As RTF derivative after the protection-loss warning
native encrypted source DOC with a typed SttbfAssoc write-reservation value
native encrypted source DOCX with an OOXML w:writeProtection record

native_reopen.prompt_text_fragment: reserved by Ryker Zhu Enter the password to modify ... or open read only
native_reopen.interpretation: The RTF is plaintext and no longer has password-to-open encryption, while native Word still recognizes a modify reservation.

structural_passwordhash_compatibility_pr.probe: PasswordHash::from_bytes on the same decoded writereservhash bytes
structural_passwordhash_compatibility_pr.warning: This is a byte-layout probe only. The writereservhash parser stores the record as opaque WriteReservationHash bytes and does not assert PasswordHash semantics or verify a credential.

temporary_copy_without_empty_datastore.tolerance_report: not applicable to this raw-model probe

boundary_order: writereservhash is recognized and decoded before the later root datastore group.
The direct original parse fails at the empty datastore before a complete Document is returned.
After only the datastore group is removed, the raw typed model retains the exact 120-byte hash.

write_reservation.reader_result: pass; five-paragraph story and markers retained in memory

doc.interpretation: The encrypted DOC keeps a plaintext typed modify-password string in the decrypted associated-string table in addition to password-to-open encryption.

typed_reader_projection.reader_result: pass; five paragraphs and markers retained in memory

docx.interpretation: The encrypted DOCX stores a hashed modify-password record in word/settings.xml. litchi-docx exposes the write-protection boolean but not the raw hash and salt through its typed settings projection.

rtf.outer_encryption: none observed; the RTF is plaintext and contains no passwordhash/password controls
rtf.write_reservation: one native writereservhash record retained as 120 opaque bytes
rtf.typed_reader_projection: raw litchi-rtf model retains the bytes only after the unrelated empty datastore group is isolated

facts: Native Word info and root header precede one starred writereservhash destination.
The writereservhash control begins at byte offset 16541 and its hexadecimal payload is 240 characters / 120 decoded bytes.
The five source content markers survive in the plaintext RTF body.
The root ends with one empty starred datastore group.
The DOC CryptoAPI and DOCX Agile profiles were decrypted only in memory.
The DOC SttbfAssoc write-reservation slot is typed as Office42!.
The encrypted source hashes, stream sizes, and five story markers are recorded.
Root-level writereservhash is dispatched before visible text and duplicate destinations are rejected.
The writereservhash destination accepts only an even hexadecimal text payload and converts it to opaque bytes.
WriteReservationHash stores Cow<[u8]> and validates only non-empty and bounded data; it never authenticates or decrypts the value.
An empty starred datastore payload is a hard MalformedDocument error.
PasswordHash has an independent fixed-header parser; accepting the RTF writereservhash bytes with it is recorded only as a structural compatibility probe.

expected.error: MalformedDocument("RTF data-store payload cannot be empty")

machine_checkable_expectations.operation: Remove only the exact empty datastore group in a temporary file outside the repository, then open with litchi_rtf::raw::Document.

native_ui_follow_ups.expected_difference: Compare whether Word emits the same 120-byte writereservhash layout when no source open-encryption downgrade is involved.
native_ui_follow_ups.purpose: Separate the RTF modify-reservation producer from the encrypted-DOC-to-RTF downgrade path.

native_ui_follow_ups.ui_authoring: Save an otherwise identical native Word document as RTF with both open and modify password fields blank.
native_ui_follow_ups.expected_difference: Use raw control counts and native modify-prompt behavior to establish the absence baseline for writereservhash.
native_ui_follow_ups.purpose: Confirm the single starred hash group is caused by the modify-password choice.

hypotheses.label: hypothesis
hypotheses.statement: The 120-byte native writereservhash payload uses the same fixed byte layout as the library's modern PasswordHash record: version 2, total size 120, flags 0x18, algorithm id 0x800e, spin count 100000, 16-byte salt, 64-byte logical hash, and 12 trailing bytes.
evidence: The byte-level PasswordHash::from_bytes probe accepts the complete payload and reports those fields.
The payload's declared total size equals its decoded length.
The litchi-rtf writereservhash model intentionally retains the same bytes opaquely and does not make this semantic assertion.

hypotheses.label: hypothesis
hypotheses.statement: The native Save As RTF operation preserved modify-reservation metadata while dropping the source DOC/DOCX password-to-open envelope.
evidence: The RTF is a plaintext ANSI file with no passwordhash/password controls.
Native Word reopened the RTF without a password-to-open prompt but displayed a modify-reservation prompt naming Ryker Zhu.
The source DOC and DOCX independently contain password-to-open encryption and modify-reservation records.

negative_expectations.expectation: Do not report a successful direct litchi-rtf parse of the native RTF.
negative_expectations.reason: The unmodified fixture fails before semantic counts at the empty datastore destination.

negative_expectations.expectation: Do not treat PasswordHash::from_bytes acceptance as password verification or as proof that writereservhash and passwordhash have identical authentication semantics.
negative_expectations.reason: The compatibility probe is structural; WriteReservationHash is documented and implemented as inert opaque bytes.

negative_expectations.expectation: Do not infer that the DOCX typed settings boolean exposes or verifies the hash and salt.
negative_expectations.reason: The decrypted XML contains raw hash/salt attributes, while litchi-docx's typed settings projection reports only is_write_protected.

limitations: The exact native protection-loss warning text is recorded, but the exact UI control or actor that confirmed it was not observed; the final RTF save itself was observed after human approval.
The semantic RTF values in this record come from a temporary copy with only the empty datastore group removed. The native fixture itself was never edited.
The structural passwordhash-compatible field split is a diagnostic interpretation, not a claim that the RTF writereservhash value can be used by litchi or any caller to authenticate Office42!.
The DOCX clear OPC package and the DOC decrypted streams were inspected in memory only; no clear derivative was written to disk.
This is coverage for the finalized native Word build and fixture identified by rtf-487; it does not generalize to other Word versions, RTF producers, or alternate reservation algorithms.
No library source, Office fixture, or common coverage manifest was modified by this inspection.
